name: Precedent
description: Evidence-gated evaluation of Skill Workshop drafts: every skill proposal is graded by a deterministic offline checker (integrity digests, secret scan, uncited-verification claims, machine-scope leakage, dropped safety requirements, risk deltas, size) before it is applied. Fail-closed by default.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Grade skill proposals. When false the evaluator stays registered but returns `pass` without spawning anything, so its absence is visible in the proposal record instead of silent.

pythonBin.title: Python interpreter
pythonBin.description: Fallback interpreter, used as `<pythonBin> -m precedent` when `precedentBin` is not on PATH. Point it at a virtualenv's python (…/.venv/bin/python) if precedent is installed there rather than globally.

precedentBin.title: Precedent CLI
precedentBin.description: The precedent executable, resolved from PATH unless an absolute path is given. Installed by `pipx install precedent-cli`.

failClosed.title: Fail closed
failClosed.description: What to do when the evaluator itself fails — missing binary, crash, timeout, unparseable output. true = block the proposal; false = downgrade to `revise`. Leave this on: OpenClaw records a thrown error or a hook timeout as an attributed error outcome and applies the proposal anyway, so an evaluator that fails open is an evaluator that silently approves. This setting never weakens a real verdict; a `block` earned by a finding blocks either way.

timeoutMs.title: CLI timeout (ms)
timeoutMs.description: Hard wall-clock limit on the grading subprocess. The hook registration asks OpenClaw for this plus 15 s of headroom, so that a subprocess timeout always comes back as an explicit decision instead of losing the race to OpenClaw's own hook timeout (which does not block).

blockOn.title: Block on
blockOn.description: Lowest severity that vetoes an apply. `critical` (default) blocks integrity mismatches, live credentials, fabricated verification claims, dropped safety requirements and exfiltration shapes, and lets `warn` through as `revise`. `warn` is the strict setting: anything short of clean is refused.

maxBundleBytes.title: Max bundle bytes
maxBundleBytes.description: Refuse to grade a candidate bundle larger than this rather than paying to serialise it. The core already flags a bundle over 1 MiB as a size defect, so a bundle over this cap is pathological — usually a binary asset that does not belong in a skill.
